messages:
Connor O'Brien: Putting together rollout plan for SIEM-ready audit export beta enablement. Need: (a) feature flag steps, (b) canary tenants, (c) rollback conditions. Looping @Talia Benson @Naomi Feldman @Priya Natarajan @Sean Gallagher.

Talia Benson: :eyes: yep. we should align on exact sequencing + who presses the button.

Naomi Feldman: +1. also need to reflect the beta contract language: “enabled by flag per tenant, may be paused/disabled if instability”.

Benji Okafor: Flag is implemented in control plane (PR #28445) as per-tenant allowlist with a denylist override. Default OFF. Console page also hidden behind `console.security.audit_export_beta`.

Connor O'Brien: Great. Proposed steps:
1) Staging: enable flag for `tnt_staging_canary` + run automated test event to each sink (Splunk/Datadog/S3)
2) Prod internal dogfood: enable for Redwood internal workspace (if we can route to dev Splunk)
3) Prod canary: 1-2 external tenants, limited destinations
4) Expand: add remaining beta tenants in batches

Need to confirm canary tenant IDs + constraints.

Priya Natarajan: For internal dogfood: we can use the Redwood sandbox org, but note we don’t want to ship any real security events externally. We should generate synthetic audit events only (test endpoint already in exporter?) and route to internal Splunk index.

Felix Schneider: Console has “Send test event” button wired to `POST /audit-export/destinations/{id}:test` in #28411. It sends a synthetic `audit.export.test` event (no PII). So dogfood works.

Marcus Lin: Please make sure the “test event” is explicitly marked in schema (event_type = `audit.export.test`) and includes `redaction = true` / no actor email. Also audit log the config changes + test sends (we want traceability for enabling/disabling).

Benji Okafor: Config changes are audited (`audit.export.destination.created/updated/deleted`, `audit.export.destination.enabled/paused`) in #28427. Test sends currently produce `audit.export.test` + also a `audit.export.test_requested` control-plane event. (We can confirm names; might be slightly different in latest build.)

Connor O'Brien: Ok. Canary tenants suggestion (from PM beta shortlist):
- Stonewire Software (Dedicated, Splunk)
- Echelon Health (Hosted, Datadog)
- Altitude Defense (Private, S3)
Northbridge Financial (Splunk) feels higher risk; maybe not first canary.

Naomi Feldman: Agree on not starting w/ Northbridge.
Stonewire + Echelon are good coverage for hosted/dedicated and 2 sinks.
Altitude is Private so rollout mechanics differ; maybe we do them as a separate “installer canary” vs feature flag canary.

Diego Santos: +1. Private enablement is gated by chart values + network egress anyway. The per-tenant flag is irrelevant in fully private unless they’re using our control plane. We should treat Private as a separate track: “installer version X includes exporter; default disabled; customer explicitly opts in”.

Sean Gallagher: For rollback: we need concrete conditions. From SRE side I want:
- paging if delivery success rate < 99.9% over 30m for any sink (excluding customer auth failures)
- paging if p95 end-to-end delivery latency > 10m for 30m (hosted/dedicated)
- warning if backlog depth > 2h worth of events OR DLQ growth > N/min
Rollback trigger could be “2 pages in 1h” or “SLO burn > 2x for 30m”.

Rafael Mendes: Also add a “connector retry storm” guard: if retry rate spikes (e.g., >5% of batches retrying for 15m) we should pause that destination automatically (state=DEGRADED/PAUSED) vs leaving it to hammer.

Benji Okafor: We have a circuit breaker in worker: after consecutive 5xx/timeouts it flips destination into `degraded` and backs off; manual pause still possible via API. Auto-pause threshold is configurable; right now it’s conservative.

Allison Grant: For rollout we should have dashboard links ready before we flip any prod flags. The observability pack has:
- `audit_export_delivery_success_total{sink=...}`
- `audit_export_delivery_latency_seconds` histogram
- `audit_export_backlog_events` + `audit_export_backlog_seconds_estimate`
- `audit_export_dlq_events_total`
I’ll drop the dashboard URL once prod is deployed.

Connor O'Brien: Cool. Release plan detail (draft):

A) Preconditions (prod):
- dashboards deployed + alerts enabled (in “ticket-only” mode first?)
- runbook link in alert annotations
- on-call ownership confirmed (SRE primary, platform secondary)
- verify feature flag service reachable from control plane

B) Rollout steps (prod hosted/dedicated):
0. Keep exporter workers running but no destinations enabled (safe idle)
1. Enable console flag for internal only
2. Enable per-tenant flag for Redwood internal sandbox tenant
3. Add 1 canary customer tenant (Stonewire) allowlist; enable only Splunk destination; leave filters narrow (admin/auth events only) for first 24h
4. Add 2nd canary tenant (Echelon) allowlist; enable only Datadog destination
5. If stable 48h: add remaining beta tenants (batch size 2/day)

C) Rollback conditions:
- any incident impacting primary API latency attributed to export workers => immediate disable flags + pause all destinations
- sustained 5xx from connector causing backlog to exceed 2h estimate in 60m for >=1 tenant => pause destination(s), remove tenant from allowlist
- schema validation errors > 0.1% events in 15m => rollback exporter version + disable new tenant enables

Does that match expectations?

Naomi Feldman: Looks good. One nuance: messaging to customers says at-least-once. Duplicates are not rollback-worthy by themselves unless we see unbounded duplication (bug) vs expected retry dupes.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. “Duplicate rate” is a metric but not immediate rollback unless it’s runaway.

Marcus Lin: Another rollback condition: any evidence of cross-tenant leakage (wrong tenant_id in payload / wrong destination receiving events) => emergency disable + security incident. That should be explicit.

Connor O'Brien: Yep, adding that as “SEV0, immediate kill switch”.

Chloe Martin: For console gating: our flag is separate from backend flag. If backend enabled but console hidden, customers can still use API/terraform to configure destinations. Is that ok? For beta we probably want both gated, but we should assume some customers will use terraform.

Priya Natarajan: We should gate at API level too (control plane returns 403 unless tenant flag enabled). That’s what #28445 does I think.

Benji Okafor: Correct: destination CRUD endpoints check `feature.audit_export_beta` (tenant flag). Console flag only affects visibility/UX. So API is safe.

Talia Benson: Who owns the actual allowlist updates? release eng or platform?

Connor O'Brien: I’d prefer platform on-call does the allowlist changes (they’re closest to the service), but release will coordinate timing + checklist.

Priya Natarajan: Platform can do it. Let’s document exact commands + where allowlist lives (admin endpoint vs config repo).

Benji Okafor: It’s an internal admin endpoint: `POST /internal/feature-flags/audit_export_beta/allowlist` (auth restricted). I’ll paste exact curl + required scopes in the release checklist.

release-bot: Deploy notice: `redwood-control-plane` build 2025.02.09.3 scheduled for prod at 22:00 UTC. Includes PRs: #28411 #28427 #28445.

Allison Grant: Dashboard is live in prod now: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/audit-export/overview (internal). Alerts are in “notify #eng-sre only” mode.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: after first canary flip, let’s turn paging ON for: backlog>2h, DLQ growth, success rate. We can keep latency paging off until we see baseline.

Sean Gallagher: I’m ok with that. Baseline first 24h, then harden.

Connor O'Brien: Canaries (confirming):
- Stonewire: `tnt_9f3a2c` (Dedicated) Splunk
- Echelon: `tnt_2b17de` (Hosted) Datadog
(Altitude later via Private installer track)
Naomi/Talia can you confirm those tenant IDs from CS? I only have them from earlier notes.

Talia Benson: I’ll confirm w/ Colin + Fatima and reply here.

Naomi Feldman: Also, for Stonewire: they asked about “include only admin changes + API key events” initially. So filter preset should be conservative.

Felix Schneider: Console supports filter templates. We can pre-fill: include `auth.*`, `rbac.*`, `api_key.*`, `audit.export.*` and exclude high-volume inference request events.

Marcus Lin: Please ensure we’re not exporting prompt content / user content. Audit schema v1 should never include that but it’s worth sanity-checking the event types included.

Priya Natarajan: The export pipeline consumes only audit log stream, not request logs. Still, filter defaults should avoid noisy types (e.g., `inference.request.*` shouldn’t exist in audit anyway).

Connor O'Brien: Action items:
- Benji: paste allowlist update commands + rollback steps (remove allowlist, pause destinations)
- Allison: confirm alert thresholds + which are paging vs notify-only for canary window
- Talia: confirm tenant IDs + customer readiness date
- Naomi/Marcus: confirm “SEV0 security rollback” language for runbook

Tentative enablement time: after control plane deploy + 24h bake, flip internal dogfood, then Stonewire next business day.

Talia Benson: works. I’ll aim to confirm IDs today.

Allison Grant: I’ll propose alert thresholds in the SRE thread and link here.

Benji Okafor: I’ll add an internal doc snippet + also make sure “pause destination” is surfaced in Console (button should call `POST ...:pause`).

Sean Gallagher: Once canary is live, please post the dashboard screenshot + last_success_at for each destination here. Helps on-call.

Connor O'Brien: Will do. :shipit:
